pages.text:
I'm not feeling so good, Mom.
Let's visit Dr Bongi.
She can help.
pages.change: Alex tells Mom he feels unwell and she decides to take him to Dr Bongi
pages.page_turn_note: Dialogue with no tags; the turn moves to the clinic.

notes: Alex holds his tummy on an orange rug beside a toy car; Mom sits cross-legged, concerned; her line is in a speech bubble over a sky and flowers
illustration.only_in_image: He holds his tummy: where he feels ill is only in the picture, and who says which line is shown only by the speech bubble.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Drink this medicine, Alex.
It will make you feel better.
But I don't like
medicine. It's yucky.
pages.change: The doctor prescribes medicine; Alex thinks it is yucky
pages.page_turn_note: His refusal is a thought, not spoken; the turn shows his first dodge.

notes: Dr Bongi in a white coat holds out a bottle with a red cross; Alex sits on Mom's lap; a huge medicine bottle fills a thought cloud on a red page
illustration.only_in_image: His objection is drawn as a thought cloud, not speech: he never tells the doctor; and the bottle in his mind is drawn huge on an alarm-red page.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Jett, I'll let you
play with my
shiny red car if
you drink my
medicine.
Eeew, no way!
pages.change: Alex offers Jett his red car if Jett drinks the medicine; Jett refuses
pages.page_turn_note: The bribe fails within the spread.

notes: Alex holds up the car and the bottle; Jett stands with arms crossed, frowning
illustration.only_in_image: Jett is a younger-looking boy with arms crossed; the same boy is later at home with Mom, which suggests a brother (INFERRED).

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
How can I make my medicine
taste better?
I know, I'll put it on my sandwich.
pages.change: He wonders how to make it taste better and decides to put it on his sandwich
pages.page_turn_note: The idea spread ends on a plan; the turn shows the result in one word and a picture.

notes: question marks over a thinking face; a yellow page with a white lightbulb shape framing the imagined plan around a towering sandwich

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.page_turn_note: One interjection; the picture carries the failure.

notes: a close-up of Alex's shocked face on a lime page; the sandwich collapses under green goo with tomato slices flying
illustration.only_in_image: The sandwich is drowned in green medicine and falls apart: what went wrong is only in the picture; the text is one cry.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Maybe I should hide it away.
I know, I'll hide it in the garden.
pages.change: He decides to hide the medicine in the garden
pages.page_turn_note: Second idea spread; the reader now expects a failure after the turn.

notes: question marks again; a yellow page with a white lightbulb shape framing the imagined plan around the bottle buried in a hole with a small rake

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.page_turn_note: Cry plus a picture of the culprit.

notes: Alex's hands cover his mouth on a lime page; a dog with a muddy nose holds the dug-up bottle in its mouth
illustration.only_in_image: The family dog has dug the bottle up and carries it in its mouth; the dog is not mentioned in the text.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
I'd better try something else.
I know, I'll hide it in a bird's nest.
pages.change: He decides to hide the medicine in a bird's nest
pages.page_turn_note: Third idea spread; his face is more doubtful each time.

notes: a worried, doubtful face; a yellow page with a white lightbulb shape framing the imagined plan around a nest with three speckled eggs and the bottle
illustration.only_in_image: His face is more doubtful than on the earlier idea spreads (raised brows, open mouth).

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.page_turn_note: The third failure closes the pattern of three.

notes: Alex gasps on a lime page; a bird returning to the nest kicks the bottle out with its foot
illustration.only_in_image: The mother bird kicks the bottle out of her nest; the bird is not named in the text.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Hmm, maybe I should
just try it?
pages.change: He wonders whether he should just try it, and the picture shows him taking it
pages.page_turn_note: A self-question on the left; the right shows the dose; the turn reveals what it feels like.

notes: left: Alex looks at the bottle uncertainly; right: Mom gives him a spoonful on her lap, Jett holds a teddy and covers his mouth, the dog watches; a thought cloud shows Alex with a caped bottle and the car
illustration.only_in_image: Mom gives him the dose on a spoon on her lap, with Jett and the dog watching: the text only has his question, and the picture shows that an adult gives the medicine.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Wooah, this is
actually so much fun!
I feel something...
What's happening?
pages.change: The medicine turns into a fun imagined ride; he feels something happening
pages.page_turn_note: Ends on a direct question answered after the turn.

notes: Alex floats on his back in a green sea; the dog swims; the rake, a pickle, a lettuce leaf, the bird, the red car, a tomato and an egg float around them
illustration.only_in_image: The medicine becomes a green sea he floats in, and every object from his failed plans (sandwich pieces, rake, bird, egg, car) floats in it with the dog.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
I feel
so much
better!
And all I had
to do was drink
my medicine.
You did it, Alex!
We're so proud of you.
pages.change: He feels much better and Mom says they are proud of him
pages.page_turn_note: Last story spread; the book closes on an unworded vignette.

notes: Alex stands in a red cape, green drips at the hem, at the end of the green wave; Mom laughs with Jett and the dog on the rug; the bottle and toy car on the rug
illustration.only_in_image: He wears a red superhero cape dripping green: the super of the title is shown, not said.

pages.label: OBSERVED
